title: Zuriel Chapter Introductions — Psalms 31–60

chapters.title: Psalm 31 — A prayer for refuge
chapters.historicalContext: Psalm 31 belongs to Israel's prayer and worship collection. A lament entrusts life to God while facing danger and betrayal.
chapters.overview: The prayer joins distress with confidence and asks for rescue without denying vulnerability.
chapters.studyObservation: Attend to the psalm's movement, images and speaker. The prayer joins distress with confidence and asks for rescue without denying vulnerability.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read Psalm 31 as a complete poem, noticing its opening, turning point and conclusion. Compare its theme with nearby psalms without assuming they share one setting.
studyQuestions: What emotion, situation or act of worship shapes this prayer?
Which images or repeated words carry the main message?
How can this psalm shape faithful prayer without turning its poetry into an unconditional promise?
chapters.lifeApplication: Let this psalm form honest prayer, wise action and compassion. A lament entrusts life to God while facing danger and betrayal.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: The prayer joins distress with confidence and asks for rescue without denying vulnerability.

chapters.historicalContext: Psalm 57 belongs to Israel's prayer and worship collection. The psalm celebrates refuge and asks God to act against persistent violence.
chapters.overview: The strong language belongs to a plea for justice and must not be converted into permission for retaliation.
chapters.studyObservation: Attend to the psalm's movement, images and speaker. The strong language belongs to a plea for justice and must not be converted into permission for retaliation.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read Psalm 57 as a complete poem, noticing its opening, turning point and conclusion. Compare its theme with nearby psalms without assuming they share one setting.
studyQuestions: What emotion, situation or act of worship shapes this prayer?
Which images or repeated words carry the main message?
How can this psalm shape faithful prayer without turning its poetry into an unconditional promise?
